summary.tldr: Requires the federal government to develop and report on a national strategy for children and youth in Canada, with goals on poverty, mental health, living standards and rights.
what_it_does: Requires the minister to develop a national strategy for children and youth in Canada.

Requires the strategy to set goals, including ending child poverty, improving access to mental health services, raising living standards, and meeting listed children's, Indigenous and disability rights commitments.

Requires the strategy to include measurable outcomes, evidence-based assessments, a plan for unmet goals, resource needs, public monitoring, complaint handling, updates for new needs, and parliamentary oversight.

Requires the minister to consult children and youth, relevant federal, provincial and municipal officials, Indigenous governing bodies, and other stakeholders, using culturally safe and language-accessible consultations.
Requires progress reports to Parliament every six months until the strategy is tabled within 24 months, then review reports every five years after that.
who_it_affects: First Nations, Inuit and Métis children and youth
summary.background: The bill creates a federal requirement to develop a national strategy for children and youth and sets rules for consultation, reporting and later review.
